tips.title: 🏠 Mortgage Tips
tips.tip1: A 20% down payment helps you avoid PMI
tips.tip2: Consider 15-year loans for lower total interest costs
tips.tip3: Shop around with multiple lenders for the best rates
tips.tip4: Factor in closing costs (typically 2-5% of loan amount)
tips.tip5: Get pre-approved to strengthen your offer
tips.tip6: Consider property taxes and insurance in your budget

homeAffordabilityCalculator.title: Home Affordability Calculator
homeAffordabilityCalculator.description: Calculate how much house you can afford based on your income, debts, and financial situation
homeAffordabilityCalculator.monthlyDebtsDesc: Include student loans, car payments, credit cards, etc.
homeAffordabilityCalculator.frontEndRule: Front-end ratio: Housing costs ≤ 28% of gross income
homeAffordabilityCalculator.backEndRule: Back-end ratio: Total debt payments ≤ 36% of gross income
homeAffordabilityCalculator.guidelinesNote: These are guidelines - actual approval depends on credit, assets, and loan type
homeAffordabilityCalculator.fhaNote: FHA loans may allow higher ratios (up to 43% back-end)
homeAffordabilityCalculator.creditScoreFactor: Credit Score: Higher scores get better rates
homeAffordabilityCalculator.dtiFactor: Debt-to-Income: Lower DTI = more buying power
homeAffordabilityCalculator.interestRateFactor: Interest Rates: Even 0.5% makes a big difference
homeAffordabilityCalculator.locationFactor: Location: Property taxes and insurance vary
homeAffordabilityCalculator.estimateNote: This calculator provides estimates - actual loan approval depends on many factors
homeAffordabilityCalculator.maintenanceNote: Budget for maintenance (1-3% of home value annually)
homeAffordabilityCalculator.emergencyFundNote: Keep an emergency fund separate from your down payment
homeAffordabilityCalculator.preApprovalNote: Get pre-approved before house hunting for accurate numbers
homeAffordabilityCalculator.ownershipCostsNote: Consider all homeownership costs: utilities, repairs, upgrades

formulas.powerFormula: HP per Pound = Horsepower ÷ Vehicle Weight (lbs)
formulas.weightFormula: Pounds per HP = Vehicle Weight (lbs) ÷ Horsepower
formulas.note: Power to weight ratio is a key indicator of vehicle performance. Higher ratios generally mean better acceleration and performance, but other factors like aerodynamics, traction, and gearing also play important roles.
